title: Research Question
text:
The Impact of AI Permission on Cognitive Performance and Confidence in College Students
PAGE 1
Research Question
▪ How does explicitly 
permitting AI use 
affect college students' 
CRT-2 logic performance, 
self-reported 
AI/outside-assistance 
use, and their 
performance confidence?
By: Madison, Andy and Rayna

title: Background & Support
text:
Background & Support
Past Research Findings:
● High AI reliance can impair critical thinking, often 
due to cognitive fatigue (Tian & Zhang, 2025).
○ However, strong AI literacy acts as a buffer 
against negative cognitive and psychological 
learning effects (Tian & Zhang, 2025).
What is Cognitive Fatigue?
The fried feeling that happens when you constantly 
read, tweak, and double-check AI outputs.
Common Signs: brain fog, decision paralysis: 
AI usage itself isn't detrimental; its effects depend on 
how it's used.
We will examine how formal permission for AI use alters students' 
usage, logic capabilities, and self-reported confidence.
Background & Support PAGE 2

title: Variables & Study Design
text:
Variables
Independent Variables (IVs)
1.) AI Usage Permitted (Between-subjects, 
manipulated)
-Level 1: AI-Permitted, Level 2: (Control) No AI 
mention
2.) Gender
-Level 1: Male, Level 2: Female, Level 3: 
Non-Binary/Prefer not to say
3.) Grouping Variable: Self-Reported Outside 
Assistance Use
-Level 1: Reported AI Assistance, Level 2: Reported 
No Assistance
Dependent Variables (DVs)
1.) Actual Performance: Their score on 
Cognitive Reflection Test (2) (CRT-2) logic 
puzzles
-4-item logic task scoring actual performance 
on tricky questions (enforced with timer, 
minimize AI use)
2.) Perceived Performance: Self-rated 
confidence and performance scale
-Questions asking how confident participant 
feels they performed
Design
Between-subjects (random 
assignment to AI Usage condition)
PAGE 3Background & Support Variables Hypothesis

title: Hypotheses
text:
Hypothesis
▪Participants in the Group who are explicitly given permission to use AI will be more likely to report using it than those in the control group who were not given any mention of AI use for the logic task.▪Students who report using AI or outside help will score higher on the logic test (CRT) than those who do not (Note: this is a correlational observation, not a causal one.)▪The group permitted to use AI, or who choose to use it, will report higher confidence in their performance.▪We will explore if there are any gender differences in the use of AI, the logic task performance and confidence, to see if there is any significant difference in gender.
